approaches.name: Stock-to-Flow / S2FX Scarcity Power-Law
approaches.description: S2F models Bitcoin's market value as a power-law function of its stock-to-flow ratio (existing supply / annual new issuance), the same monetary-scarcity metric used for gold and silver. PlanB's original fit was ln(market value) = 3.3·ln(SF) + 14.6, i.e. value ∝ SF^3.3, reportedly R²≈0.95; the later S2FX cross-asset version pools BTC/gold/silver and treats halvings as discrete "phase transitions" (clusters), reportedly R²≈0.997. A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: because Bitcoin's issuance halves every ~4 years, SF roughly doubles each halving, so the power law projects ~10x market value per doubling. Chaining that across the ~2028, ~2032, ~2036 halvings yields the model's forward price path and hence an implied multi-year appreciation rate — purely supply-driven, with no role for demand, cashflow, volatility, or cross-asset correlation.
key_drivers: Stock-to-flow ratio SF = circulating supply / annual new issuance (rises mechanically as block subsidy halves every ~210,000 blocks / ~4 years)
Power-law exponent (~3.3 in original S2F) linking ln(SF) to ln(market value)
Halving schedule — the deterministic, pre-programmed supply shock that doubles SF and drives ~10x value steps
Cross-asset anchoring: gold (SF~62) and silver (SF~22) market values used to pin the regression line and justify a 'monetary scarcity' premium for BTC as SF approaches/exceeds gold
Phase transitions / clusters (S2FX): treating each halving epoch as a regime with distinct properties, replacing time with SF as the independent variable
Absolute scarcity / 21M hard cap as the terminal narrative (SF → ∞ as issuance → 0)
pros: Fully deterministic supply input: the halving schedule and 21M cap are known in advance, so SF is the rare financial variable with zero forecast error — attractive for a long-horizon CMA skeleton
Parsimonious and falsifiable: a single regressor produces explicit, dated price targets that can be checked (and have been)

Captures a real economic intuition — that a credibly fixed, ungrowable supply supports a monetary 'hardness' premium (the same logic that makes gold a store of value); the Austrian/Mises critique even concedes SF can matter for a money's quality
Cross-asset framing (S2FX) at least disciplines the BTC fit against gold and silver rather than fitting BTC in isolation

Morillon & Chacon (2022), the first peer-reviewed treatment, find the in-sample fit is robust to early-assumption choices (not pure data-mining) and that dynamic out-of-sample accuracy improves over time
cons: Spurious regression / non-stationarity: both ln(price) and ln(SF) are non-stationary, trending series, so the high R² is the textbook artifact of regressing one trend on another. Without cointegration the coefficients and R² are statistically meaningless (Burger, Bitcoinwords/WORDS review; has been shown cointegration generally does not hold)
SF is a near-deterministic step function of time, so S2F is effectively price-regressed-on-time in disguise — it cannot distinguish scarcity from any other variable that trended up over 2010-2020

Demand-blind by construction: ignores adoption, liquidity, ETF flows, macro/real rates, regulation. Mises critique: scarcity (a subjective demand condition) is conflated with the mechanical SF ratio; price comes from marginal valuations, not a physical supply metric

Out-of-sample failure: PlanB's S2F/S2FX predicted >$100k for 2021-2022; BTC closed Nov-2021 ~$57k and bottomed <$16k in 2022. The model has traded materially below trend since 2021 (off by ~$130k at points). 'Floor model' walk-back further eroded credibility

Diminishing-returns problem: S2F implies a constant ~10x per halving forever (no decay), contradicting the clear empirical decay of BTC's growth rate (142%→65%→17%/yr) — the model is structurally too bullish at long horizons and its targets (e.g. $288k, $500k+, eventually multi-million) are unbounded
Even when the fit 'works', Morillon & Chacon show an S2F-timing strategy underperforms buy-and-hold — no economic value added
Says nothing about volatility or correlations — it is a price-level model only, so it cannot directly populate most CMA cells (vol, corr to equities/FI/TIPS/gold)
S2FX 'phase transitions' have only ~4-6 data clusters; fitting a power law through 4 points (plus gold/silver) is gross overfitting and 'has not been replicated or reviewed' per PlanB himself

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: Not published as an annualized rate; S2F/S2FX publishes price-level targets implying ~10x market value per halving (~78%/yr compounded). Specific targets: ~$55k (post-2020 halving, original S2F) and $288k (S2FX next cluster, 2020-2024); later PlanB commentary cites $500k+. None realized on schedule.
cited_outputs.appreciation_real: n/a (source silent — model is nominal-USD price only; no inflation adjustment)
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a (source silent — S2F/S2FX is a deterministic price-level model and makes no volatility statement)
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a as a correlation; but the S2FX thesis explicitly places BTC on the SAME scarcity regression line as gold (gold SF~62, silver SF~22), asserting a structural co-valuation rather than a measured correlation. (Morillon & Chacon report S2F R²≈0.95; S2FX R²≈0.997 — fit, not correlation to other assets.)

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~12-18%/yr (judgment, not a model output). S2F's own logic says ~10x/halving (~78%/yr) forever, but that is the model's central flaw; imposing the empirically-required appreciation decay (realized 142%→65%→17% over full/10y/5y windows) and the fact that BTC's SF will soon exceed gold's — removing the 'catch-up to gold' leg that powered past returns — collapses the forward rate to roughly a low-double-digit monetary-debasement-plus-marginal-adoption pace. I deliberately discount the model's literal targets ($288k-$500k+).
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~9-15%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run CPI). Reflects BTC as a maturing scarce asset whose excess return compresses toward a gold-like-but-higher store-of-value premium.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment; S2F is silent, so anchored to realized trailing-5y/10y vol of 57%/69%). The floor sits AT realized ~57% — the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized — with a defensible decade-average band of ~50-60%. Vol stays multiples of equities.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: +0.45 to +0.60 (judgment; S2F is silent so anchored to realized trailing-5y corr of 0.56, which has risen as BTC institutionalized into risk-asset portfolios). Note this directly contradicts the model's 'pure scarcity, demand-independent' premise.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: +0.30 to +0.40 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.37)
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: +0.15 to +0.25 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.19 — modestly positive via shared duration/liquidity sensitivity)
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: +0.25 to +0.35 (judgment; realized trailing-5y 0.30; real-rate sensitivity shared with other long-duration stores of value)
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10 (judgment). S2FX bills BTC as 'digital scarcity' that should co-move with gold, but realized correlation is essentially zero (-0.01 full / +0.03 10y / +0.045 5y). I keep it in the 0.0-0.10 band, NOT the higher 'digital-gold' linkage the model implies. Internal contradiction worth naming: a scarcity thesis that says BTC absorbs gold's monetary role REQUIRES co-movement to justify the share transfer, yet the data shows none — you cannot simultaneously claim 'BTC takes gold's monetary share' and treat the near-zero realized gold correlation as comfortable. The honest read is that S2F's gold linkage is asserted, not measured.

approaches.name: Metcalfe's Law Network-Value (NVM)
approaches.description: This approach treats Bitcoin as a payment/communication network whose fair value scales with a power of the number of active users (wallets/addresses), per Metcalfe's Law (V proportional to n^2) or its generalizations (n*log(n) Odlyzko; or an empirically estimated exponent near 1.7). Price = (network-value function of users) / (coin supply), where supply follows the known issuance schedule (Peterson fits a Gompertz curve). A 10-15yr CMA falls out indirectly: you forecast long-run S-curve user adoption (which decelerates as the network saturates), apply the chosen Metcalfe exponent to get terminal network value, divide by terminal supply, and annualize the implied price path. Because both user growth and the per-user value multiple compress as adoption matures, the model mechanically produces decaying — not constant — forward appreciation. The relative-valuation variants (Kalichkin NVM, Wheatley-Sornette MMV) are NOT return forecasters; they only flag over/undervaluation vs current network activity and are used to time bubbles, not to set a CMA.
key_drivers: Number of active users / non-zero-balance addresses / wallets (the network size n)
Metcalfe exponent on n: classical n^2 vs Odlyzko n*log(n) vs empirically-fit ~1.7
Adoption S-curve / saturation: logistic or Gompertz user-growth path that decelerates over time (Sornette: ~35% -> 21% annual user growth over 5yr)
Coin supply schedule (Gompertz/known halving issuance) as the denominator turning network value into price
Velocity / transactional utility assumption embedded in the per-user value constant
Mean-reversion of the market-to-Metcalfe (MMV/NVM) ratio for relative timing, not level
pros: Grounds value in an observable, hard-to-fake fundamental (on-chain active users) rather than pure price extrapolation or sentiment
Parsimonious and falsifiable: a single network-size driver plus a known supply schedule; Peterson reports very high in-sample fit (R^2 ~0.93-0.95)
Naturally generates appreciation DECAY: as adoption saturates the S-curve, both user growth and value-per-user compress, so the model does not assume a constant high return forever
Relative-value variants (NVM, MMV) have demonstrated some ex-ante use flagging bubble peaks (Wheatley-Sornette identified 4 over-valuations; LPPLS bracketed crash timing)
Provides an economic mechanism (network effects) that is at least theoretically tied to utility, unlike scarcity-only models (S2F) that ignore demand entirely
cons: The headline statistical fit is largely SPURIOUS: price and active-users are both non-stationary trending series; high R^2 from log-log OLS does not survive proper time-series controls. Civitarese (2018) finds the series do NOT cointegrate and cannot reject reverse causality (price drives wallet creation, not vice versa); the Glasgow/Ledger critique shows the strong positive relationships vanish once autocorrelation and non-stationarity are handled.

Exponent is unidentified and chosen ad hoc: n^2 vs n*log(n) vs ~1.7 give wildly different terminal values, and Wheatley-Sornette show forcing the classic n^2 fits significantly WORSE than ~1.7 (p<1e-16). The CMA is highly sensitive to an arbitrary parameter.

User/address metrics are a crude, manipulable proxy: total addresses overcount (one user holds many; exchanges custody millions); active-address counts are gamed by consolidation, Lightning/L2 migration off-chain, and ETF/custodial adoption that creates ZERO new on-chain addresses — breaking the network-size signal post-2021/2024.

It is a relative/timing tool masquerading as a level forecast: Kalichkin himself states NVM forecasts CORRECTIONS not appreciation direction; using it to derive a 10-15yr return is a category error the marketing layer routinely commits.

Long-run extrapolation is explicitly unreliable — Wheatley-Sornette call long-term predictions 'effectively meaningless' because model uncertainty dominates. Practitioner forecasts ($1.5M/2035 etc.) launder a fragile in-sample fit into a precise CMA the underlying econometrics do not support.
Post-2021 structural break: institutional/ETF holdings, treasury companies and custodial concentration decouple price from on-chain active users, the model's sole driver.

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~31%/yr implied by Peterson's practitioner Metcalfe forecast of $1.5M by 2035 off a ~$100K 2025 base (10yr CAGR); peer-reviewed papers publish NO point appreciation forecast
cited_outputs.volatility: n/a (source silent) — Wheatley-Sornette characterize BTC as radically non-stationary with recurrent bubbles/crashes but publish no annualized vol figure
cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent) — Metcalfe literature models BTC purely from network size and is silent on cross-asset correlation

synthesized_outputs.appreciation_nominal: ~10-14%/yr (JUDGMENT, not a computed stat). Under Metcalfe logic the driver is active-user growth times a saturating per-user multiple. Realized BTC appreciation decayed 142%->65%->17% as it matured; an S-curve forces continued decay. Mid-single-digit-to-low-teens forward user CAGR, with the value-per-user multiple flat-to-compressing as on-chain activity migrates to L2/custodial/ETF, lands a 10-15yr nominal CMA near the low end of the realized-decay path (~10-14%), well below the practitioner ~31% which over-extrapolates an in-sample fit.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~7-11% real (subtracting ~2.5-3% long-run inflation). Judgment.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr, holding near realized ~57% across the horizon rather than declining to ~45%; far above equities/gold. Judgment, consistent with the model's emphasis on recurrent non-stationary bubbles, with the floor anchored at realized trailing-5y vol (no compression below realized yet evidenced).
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~+0.30 to +0.45. Network adoption is a risk-on/liquidity-sensitive driver, so BTC behaves like a high-beta growth/tech proxy. Judgment.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.0 to +0.15. Little fundamental link to value-equity cashflow factors. Judgment.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.0 to -0.10. Weakly negative via the discount-rate/liquidity channel; not a duration asset. Judgment.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.0 to +0.10. No real-yield mechanism in a network-size model; effectively orthogonal. Judgment.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10. The Metcalfe model implies no structural gold link at all; realized BTC-gold co-movement is ~0 (-0.01 full / +0.045 5y). I hold it at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band and explicitly reject the digital-gold reading — a network-value thesis gives no mechanism forcing gold co-movement, and the data supplies none.

approaches.name: Network Value-to-Transactions (NVT) Ratio
approaches.description: NVT treats Bitcoin like an equity P/E: network value (market cap) in the numerator, daily USD on-chain transaction volume in the denominator as a proxy for the network's "earnings"/utility throughput. The thesis is that fair value is whatever multiple of settlement activity the market is willing to pay, and that extreme NVT readings mean-revert — high NVT flags overvaluation/tops, low NVT flags undervaluation/bottoms. It is a relative-value and timing/mean-reversion framework, not a discounted-cashflow or supply-scarcity model. A 10-15yr CMA does not fall cleanly out of NVT at all: NVT produces no native long-horizon expected return. To force one, you must assume NVT mean-reverts to some equilibrium band and that real on-chain settlement value (the denominator) compounds at some growth rate over the horizon; expected appreciation then ≈ growth in transaction value ± any drift in the equilibrium multiple. Because on-chain throughput is a maturing, decelerating series (and is increasingly leaking off-chain to L2/exchanges/ETF custody), the honest NVT-consistent CMA extrapolates BTC's appreciation decay downward, not its historical level.
key_drivers: Daily on-chain USD transaction volume (the denominator / 'earnings' proxy) — its level and growth rate
Network value / market cap (numerator)
The equilibrium NVT band the market assigns and any secular drift in it
Quality of the transaction-volume measure: raw vs adjusted (stripping change outputs, self-spends, mixer/exchange-internal repetition — Coin Metrics finds raw overstates economic volume by ~3.3x)
Smoothing choice: NVT Signal (NVTS) uses a 90-day MA of volume to make the ratio a leading top/bottom indicator
Share of economic activity that stays on-chain vs migrating to Lightning/L2, centralized-exchange internal ledgers, and ETF custody (off-chain leakage degrades the denominator over time)
Velocity (NVT is effectively inverse monetary velocity), which reflects HODL vs spend behavior
pros: Intuitive analogue to a familiar equity multiple (P/E), making it communicable to traditional investors
Grounds valuation in an observable, auditable on-chain fundamental (settlement throughput) rather than pure price/sentiment
Has empirically bracketed several historical tops (high NVT) and bottoms (low NVT) ex-post, and NVT Signal added some lead time as a smoothed timing overlay
Cheap and transparent — computable from public blockchain data; Coin Metrics/Glassnode publish adjusted versions that materially clean the denominator
Conceptually forces a discipline that BTC's value should bear some relationship to its use as a settlement network, a useful counterweight to pure scarcity narratives
cons: Not a return model. NVT is a mean-reversion/timing ratio; it yields no native long-horizon expected appreciation, so any 10-15yr CMA is bolted-on assumption (denominator growth + multiple drift), not output of the framework.

Denominator is badly contaminated and structurally decaying. On-chain volume is inflated by change outputs/self-spends/mixers (raw overstates ~3.3x) AND increasingly understated as real activity moves to Lightning/L2, exchange-internal settlement, and ETF custody. Both errors are large and time-varying — the proxy for 'earnings' is breaking.

No stable equilibrium / non-comparable across regimes. Even the publishers (Glassnode) warn 2013 NVT is not one-to-one with 2021 NVT; the 'fair' band drifts, so absolute readings can't anchor valuation.

Documented in-sample failure post-2021. In 2025 NVT gave contradictory signals within one cycle (overvalued ~58 in April pre-rally; 'undervalued' near $120k in October). It is part of the broadly-failed 2024-26 cohort of on-chain top indicators (alongside MVRV Z, Pi Cycle, S2F).

Tiny sample / curve-fit risk. Calibrated on only 3-4 halving cycles; like S2F and naive Metcalfe, NVT-based valuation is fragile to regime change and lacks out-of-sample validation — academically these on-chain 'fundamentals' show weak, unstable predictive power for returns.
Circularity: market cap (numerator) is price; using a price-driven ratio to value price embeds reflexivity, especially when speculation inflates both price and on-chain churn simultaneously.
Institutionalization (ETFs) decouples price from on-chain activity entirely — the marginal buyer never touches the chain, severing the link NVT depends on.

Under NVT logic, long-run price growth should track real on-chain settlement-value growth; that throughput is maturing and leaking off-chain, so it should compound far slower than BTC's price did historically. Extrapolating the realized decay path (full-window 142% → 10y 65% → 5y 17%), I push the 10-15yr forward below the trailing-5y 17% toward roughly nominal-GDP-plus-a-modest-monetization-premium.

synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-60%/yr (judgment). Anchored to trailing-5y realized ~57% and 10y ~69%; floor held AT ~57% rather than stepped below it, because the sub-2yr ETF sample does not yet evidence compression below realized, and NVT's off-chain-leakage problem leaves fundamental value poorly pinned.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.45-0.55 (judgment). Trailing-5y realized is 0.56 and rising with ETF/institutional ownership; NVT gives no reason to expect this to fall — if anything the on-chain link weakens while the macro/risk-asset link strengthens.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.30-0.35 (judgment). Below growth-equity correlation; tracks the trailing-5y 0.37 realized, BTC behaves like a long-duration risk asset, less tied to value factor.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.15-0.25 (judgment). Low-positive, drifting up with rate-sensitivity of the marginal institutional holder (trailing-5y 0.19).
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.20-0.30 (judgment). Slightly above nominal FI; some real-rate/liquidity sensitivity, consistent with trailing-5y 0.30.

NVT framework is silent on gold, so this is pure baseline extrapolation: realized BTC-gold correlation has been near-zero historically (full-window -0.01, 5y 0.045), drifting modestly positive as both increasingly trade as macro/debasement hedges — but NVT provides no mechanism forcing co-movement, so I keep it low.

approaches.name: Cost-of-Production / Mining-Cost Floor
approaches.description: Models BTC as a "virtual commodity" whose value is anchored to the marginal cost of mining it. Hayes (2015, 2019) derives a break-even price P* = E_day / (BTC_mined_per_day), where daily energy cost E_day = (electricity $/kWh × 24h × ASIC efficiency in W/GH × hashrate) and BTC/day = θ·β·ρ/δ (block reward β, hashrate ρ, difficulty δ). In a competitive mining market, miners produce until marginal cost equals price, so the cost of production is theorized as a lower bound (floor) around which the market price "gravitates." A 10-15yr CMA does NOT fall cleanly out of this: the model produces a current floor level, not an expected return. To get a forward appreciation number you must forecast the trajectory of the floor itself — i.e., project how the four block-reward halvings, secular ASIC-efficiency gains, and the electricity-price/hashrate path push the per-coin cost up over a decade — and then assume price tracks that floor. That forecast is highly indeterminate, which is the approach's core weakness as a CMA tool.
key_drivers: Block reward β (halves every ~210k blocks / ~4yr: 6.25→3.125 BTC in Apr-2024, →1.5625 ~2028) — mechanically DOUBLES per-coin cost at each halving, the main upward driver
Mining difficulty δ / network hashrate ρ — self-adjusting every 2016 blocks to hold ~10-min block time; rises with miner entry, raising cost
ASIC energy efficiency (W/GH, J/TH) — secular technological improvement (500 W/GH in 2010-13 → <0.02 J/GH today) is the main DOWNWARD driver, partially offsetting halvings
Electricity price ($/kWh) — JPMorgan: a 1¢/kWh change moves the production-cost estimate by ~$4,300/BTC; sensitivity mechanically doubled post-2024 halving
Competitive-market marginal-cost-equals-price assumption — the load-bearing economic premise that turns a cost into a 'floor'
Difficulty-adjustment feedback loop — stabilizes cost (counteracts efficiency-driven decline) but also makes cost endogenous to price
pros: Grounds BTC in a measurable real-world input (energy), giving a concrete, refreshable dollar number rather than pure narrative — appealing to commodity-style investors
Hayes (2019) finds the marginal cost of production has statistically significant explanatory power for price; pre-2017 the market price visibly oscillated around the model price

The halving schedule is fully deterministic, so the UPWARD ratchet in per-coin cost is one of the few genuinely forecastable mechanisms in BTC valuation — gives a non-arbitrary reason to expect the floor (and thus a price tracking it) to rise over a decade
Widely used as a practitioner sentiment/valuation overlay (JPMorgan, Glassnode, MacroMicro publish a live production-cost series as an over/under-valuation gauge), so it has real desk adoption
Provides an intuitive miner-capitulation signal: when price < cash cost, weak miners shut down, difficulty falls, and the system mean-reverts — a real, observable dynamic
cons: CIRCULARITY (fatal): supply is price-INELASTIC (predetermined issuance schedule), so when price falls miners exit, difficulty drops, and cost falls to FOLLOW price. Causality runs price→cost, not cost→price. Bernstein (2026): 'the price of bitcoin is as flexible as a blob of silly putty.' This breaks the 'floor' logic that the whole CMA rests on.

The 'floor' is empirically breached in BOTH directions: price traded ~20-40% BELOW production cost for months in Oct-2022/FTX and again in Feb-2026 (price ~$70k vs cost ~$87k), while in bull runs price ran multiples ABOVE cost. So it is neither a floor nor a ceiling — at best a loose attractor.

Hayes HIMSELF cautions against imputing an intrinsic value from it: 'extreme volatility and frequent market price fluctuations… could make identifying such an intrinsic value meaningless in application.' The author disowns the strong CMA use.

Post-2017 structural break: the visible pre-2017 oscillation around the model price decoupled; with ETFs, treasury buyers, and financialization, price detached from cost. The naive model does not survive the modern regime.

Indeterminate as a return forecast: the cost floor's future level depends on the hashrate AND efficiency paths, which are themselves driven by price and AI/data-center competition for chips and power (JPMorgan notes miners now decoupling toward AI) — so the 'forecast' smuggles in a price assumption.

Tells you nothing about correlations, volatility, or risk premia — it is a level/anchor model, not a distributional CMA. All return-moment outputs must be borrowed from realized data or another framework.

Terminal contradiction: once issuance ends (~2140) there is NO marginal cost of production, yet BTC would presumably still have value — the framework cannot value the asset in the limit it is converging toward (Bernstein).

Implied trajectory only: JPMorgan-style production cost ~$18k (2023) → ~$36-40k post-2024 halving → ~$92-94k late-2025 → projected ~$180k post-2028 halving; halving mechanically doubles per-coin cost each ~4yr before efficiency offsets.

cited_outputs.corr_gold: n/a (source silent — the cost-of-production literature frames BTC as a 'virtual commodity' by analogy to gold but publishes no BTC-gold correlation)

Two halvings in a 10-15yr window each ~double the cost (~+18%/yr gross), but secular ASIC-efficiency gains and cheaper marginal power historically claw back the majority, and the realized appreciation DECAY (142%→65%→17%/yr as BTC matured) implies the floor's growth rate compresses further. Net to a high-single-digit anchor — far below realized history, consistent with a maturing-commodity cost curve.
synthesized_outputs.appreciation_real: ~3-6%/yr real (subtracting ~2.5-3% inflation). The cost floor is partly a real-energy quantity, so it should roughly preserve purchasing power plus a modest efficiency/scarcity premium.
synthesized_outputs.volatility: ~55-65%/yr (JUDGMENT). The cost model implies a slow-moving floor, but price empirically detaches far above/below cost, so realized vol stays high; floor anchored at realized trailing-5y ~57% (no compression below realized yet evidenced), top of band reflecting historical ~70-80%.
synthesized_outputs.corr_growth_eq: ~0.25-0.45 (JUDGMENT). Cost logic is correlation-agnostic, but mining capex/power demand and risk appetite tie BTC to growth/tech equities; rising as financialization deepens.
synthesized_outputs.corr_value_eq: ~0.0-0.15 (JUDGMENT). Little economic linkage between an energy-cost floor and value-factor equities.
synthesized_outputs.corr_fi_nominal: ~0.0-0.15 (JUDGMENT). Cost floor rises with energy/electricity, loosely with the price level, giving at most a weak positive tilt vs nominal bonds; effectively uncorrelated.
synthesized_outputs.corr_tips: ~0.05-0.20 (JUDGMENT). The real-energy-input framing gives a mild positive lean to real-yield/inflation-protected assets, but weak and unstable.
synthesized_outputs.corr_gold: ~0.0-0.10 (JUDGMENT). The literature analogizes BTC to gold as a mined 'virtual commodity,' which superficially argues for a higher number, but realized BTC-gold correlation is ~0. The commodity analogy is the contradiction: if BTC truly shared gold's commodity-monetary demand it would co-move with gold, yet it does not — so the cost-floor framing cannot lean on a gold linkage. I hold it at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band.

approaches.name: Power-Law Time Regression (Santostasi / Burger Corridor)
approaches.description: Models BTC price as a deterministic power law of time since genesis: P(t) = A·t^n, fit by OLS of log(price) on log(days-since-2009). The canonical fit (Santostasi/Burger) gives n≈5.6 and R²≈0.96 on a log-log chart, with parallel upper/lower "corridor" lines defining a fair-value band rather than a point estimate. A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: because annualized appreciation under P~t^n equals n/age, the model itself FORECASTS decay — ~33%/yr at today's ~17yr age, sliding to ~18%/yr by 2040 — yielding ~27% nominal CAGR over a 2026-2041 window off the central line. The corridor width (roughly -50%/+200% around fair value) supplies the dispersion/volatility view. Crucially the model is silent on volatility-as-a-stat and on cross-asset correlations; those must be imported from realized data.
key_drivers: Time since genesis (t in days) — the sole regressor
Fitted power-law exponent n≈5.6 and intercept A
Asserted network/Metcalfe feedback loop linking addresses, price, and hash-rate as mutual power laws of time
1/t appreciation decay built into the functional form
Corridor band multiples defining the fair-value dispersion
Time-origin and fit-window choices (to which the exponent is highly sensitive)
pros: Internally encodes appreciation DECAY — unlike naive 'BTC compounds at 100%+' extrapolations, the power law mechanically slows returns as the asset ages (n/age), which is the right qualitative shape for a maturing CMA

Recent peer-reviewed work (arXiv 2605.21316) finds that DESPITE weak statistical structure, the power law out-of-forecasts ARIMA, exponential smoothing and random-walk-with-drift at 12-24 month horizons (p<0.05) — so it has genuine, if modest, predictive content

Gives an explicit fair-value band (not just a point), which maps naturally onto a CMA central case plus dispersion
Author imposes a self-discipline ('do not use past ~2040'), acknowledging the model is an interpolation of an adoption S-curve, not eternal physics
cons: The headline structural claim is statistically weak: 8 of 11 Clauset-Shalizi-Newman tests REJECT the power law (lognormal preferred), and the fitted exponent varies by ~3x (α̂≈5.65 to 16.5) across reasonable shifts of the time origin — violating shift-invariance and revealing the fit is not a robust law

A 3-component sigmoid (multi-wave adoption) beats the power law in-sample on AIC/BIC — i.e., the power law is not even the best-fitting curve, it just generalizes better out-of-sample by being simpler

Any monotonically rising series looks linear on a log-log plot; log-log axes massively compress error and flatter curve-fits — the 'tight fit' is partly an axis artifact (the core critique of the Burger corridor as retrofitting, not prediction)

No economic anchor: t (calendar time) is not a value driver. The asserted Metcalfe causal loop (addresses~t^3, price~addresses^2) is the same family the academic literature largely rejects in naive form (spurious cointegration, non-stationarity), and Wheatley-Sornette's own generalized Metcalfe (exponent 1.69) is used to flag BTC as repeatedly OVER fundamental value, not to bless the trend

approaches.name: Store-of-Value / Gold-Parity TAM Substitution
approaches.description: Bitcoin is modeled not via discounted cashflows (it has none) but as an emergent monetary/store-of-value (SoV) asset competing for a slice of an existing addressable market — primarily investable gold, sometimes the broader "global market portfolio" or all SoV wealth (gold + offshore deposits + bond/sovereign-wealth hedges). The CMA is built bottom-up: (1) size the target TAM (e.g., ~$6.2T private investable gold per JPMorgan, or ~$18T total gold per ARK), (2) project that TAM's growth, (3) assume a terminal share Bitcoin captures by the horizon year (often probability-weighted across bear/base/bull adoption scenarios), (4) divide implied market cap by Bitcoin's near-fixed/asymptotic supply to get a price target, and (5) annualize price-target-over-spot into an expected CAGR. JPMorgan adds a volatility/risk-capital adjustment (Bitcoin consumes ~1.8x the risk capital of gold, so parity is on a vol-scaled, not dollar-for-dollar, basis). A 10-15yr CMA falls out directly as the annualized return from today's spot to the horizon-year probability-weighted market cap, with volatility assumed to decay toward gold-like levels and correlation to gold assumed low-to-modest (the "digital gold" thesis paradoxically does NOT require high gold correlation — it requires gold-like demand drivers).
key_drivers: Target TAM size: private investable gold (~$6.2T, JPM) vs total gold (~$18T, ARK) vs broad SoV/global-market-portfolio (~$200T, ARK)
Terminal capture share Bitcoin reaches by horizon (e.g., CF Benchmarks base 33% of gold mktcap; ARK base 2.5% / bull 6.5% of global portfolio; JPM parity = 100% of vol-adjusted private gold)
TAM growth rate (gold mktcap compounding ~3-5%/yr on CB buying + inflation)
Bitcoin's near-fixed, asymptotic supply (~21M cap, ~19.9M mined) — converts mktcap to price with minimal dilution
Volatility/risk-capital ratio vs gold (JPM: BTC ~1.8x gold's risk capital; converges as institutionalization grows)
Probability weights across bear/base/bull adoption scenarios (CF Benchmarks: 60/20/10 + 10% gold-parity)
Adoption S-curve maturity / institutional flows (ETFs, sovereign reserves, corporate treasuries) as the share-gain mechanism
pros: Theoretically coherent for a no-cashflow asset: anchors value to a measurable comparable market (gold) and a supply schedule, rather than to price-history extrapolation
Transparent and decomposable — you can stress each lever (TAM, share, weight) and the math is auditable; CF Benchmarks and ARK publish full scenario tables
Naturally produces a DECAYING expected return: as BTC's share of gold rises toward parity, marginal upside shrinks, which is the correct shape for a maturing asset's forward CMA
JPMorgan's volatility-adjustment is a genuine methodological improvement — comparing risk-capital rather than raw dollars avoids the naive 'BTC = gold mktcap' overstatement
Probability-weighting (CF Benchmarks) makes the framework usable as an actual CMA input rather than a single hype target
Supply-side is the most defensible part of the chain: Bitcoin's issuance schedule is genuinely near-deterministic
cons: The terminal capture share is an assumption, not a derivation — it is where all the optimism hides; ARK's 6.5% bull share and CF Benchmarks' 33% of gold are asserted, not estimated from any structural model

Marketing, not peer-reviewed: ARK and CF Benchmarks pieces are sell-the-asset documents from firms long Bitcoin (ARK runs ARKB; CF Benchmarks is the index provider for spot BTC ETFs) — conflict of interest is severe

The 'digital gold' premise is empirically shaky: realized BTC-gold correlation is near zero (~0.06, CF Benchmarks' own number) and BTC behaves as a high-beta risk asset, not a safe haven — it sold off WITH equities in 2022 and decoupled UPWARD from gold in 2025, contradicting the substitution thesis
JPMorgan's $170k is explicitly a 6-12 MONTH fair value, not a 10-15yr structural CMA — repurposing it as a long-horizon anchor is a category error

Gold's own market cap is not a fixed pie BTC drains from — gold demand (CB buying) and BTC demand have been positively correlated at times, so 'substitution' may be double-counting a shared macro driver (debasement/real-rate regime)

Adjacent SoV-narrative models (Stock-to-Flow, Metcalfe) that the same firms cite are largely REJECTED in the academic literature: S2F regressions are spurious — non-stationary series, serially correlated residuals, failed Engle-Granger/Johansen assumptions (Marcel Burger; ScienceDirect 2024), and S2F broke catastrophically post-2021 (predicted $100k+ during the 2022 crash to ~$16k); Metcalfe fits are over-fit and unstable out-of-sample
Path/timing risk is ignored: a probability-weighted terminal mktcap says nothing about a 70-80% drawdown en route, which a 10-15yr holder must survive
No mean-reversion anchor: if BTC overshoots gold parity, the model has no force pulling it back, unlike a DCF or yield-based valuation

approaches.name: Monetary-Substitution / M2 Elasticity & Debasement Hedge
approaches.description: This approach models Bitcoin not as a cashflow asset but as a high-beta claim on the growth of fiat money supply. The core empirical object is a cointegrating (long-run equilibrium) relationship between log BTC price and log broad money — typically US M2 or a synthetic "global M2" (sum of major-central-bank M2 converted at FX). BTC is treated as integrated of order one, I(1), and cointegrated with money: estimated long-run elasticities run ~2.0–2.65 (a 1% rise in M2 maps to a >2% rise in BTC), with a VECM error-correction term (~-0.12/month, ~5-6 month half-life) pulling price back to the money-implied "fair value." A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: forecast trend money growth, multiply by the (decaying) elasticity beta, and that is BTC's expected nominal appreciation; the debasement thesis adds that fiat dilution is the structural tailwind and BTC's fixed 21M supply (predictable issuance, ~450/day to the 2028 halving) is the differentiator vs gold.
key_drivers: Broad-money / liquidity growth (US M2 ~6%, global M2 ~7-8%) as the exogenous trend driver
BTC money-elasticity beta (~2.0-2.65 historical, must be decayed toward 1.0-1.5 forward)
Error-correction speed to money-implied fair value (~-0.12/mo, ~5-6mo half-life)
Fiscal dominance / sovereign debt growth driving fiat depreciation (the debasement premise)
Fixed transparent supply (21M cap, halvings, ~450/day issuance) as the scarcity differentiator vs both fiat and gold
Liquidity-leads-BTC lag (months); global liquidity Granger-causes BTC, raw world-M2 levels do not
pros: Grounds an otherwise cashflow-less asset in a real, testable macro variable (money supply) rather than pure sentiment or stock-to-flow numerology

Empirically the directional relationship is genuinely strong: BTC moves with global liquidity ~83% of 12-month windows (Alden/Callahan), higher than any other major asset class — a real signal, not nothing
Provides an explicit, falsifiable fair-value model (e.g. CF Benchmarks' M2 fair value) you can mark price against and that has historically mean-reverted
Conceptually clean CMA derivation: expected return = trend money growth x elasticity, which naturally forces appreciation DECAY as the elasticity compresses toward gold's
Ties BTC to the same debasement logic underwriting gold (Grayscale), making it portfolio-coherent with a real-asset / inflation-hedge sleeve
cons: The headline elasticity (2.65) and 0.94 levels-correlation are almost certainly SPURIOUS in the econometric sense: both log-BTC and log-M2 are non-stationary trending I(1) series, and naive level correlation/regression on two trends is the textbook spurious-regression trap

On contemporaneous CHANGES (the regression you should run), the M2-BTC relationship 'nearly vanishes' — correlation collapses toward ~0; the relationship lives almost entirely in shared trend, not in month-to-month co-movement

Cointegration is NOT stable: the peer-reviewed TVC-VECM literature (Park/Lee JDQS 2022) formally rejects constant coefficients (p=0.0015) in favor of smoothly time-varying ones — so a single fixed elasticity for a 10-15yr CMA is not supported by the data

Clear post-2021/2025 structural break: CF Benchmarks reports R-squared collapsing from 0.71-0.90 to ~0.59 and a ~46% fair-value gap; gold's liquidity Z-score climbed to 2.82 while BTC's fell to -1.31, i.e. the liquidity bid rotated AWAY from BTC

'Global M2' is a data-quality artifact: it is built by multiplying heterogeneous national M2 by spot FX, mixing fast- and slow-reporting regimes, and is routinely curve-fit/lag-shifted ('data torture', 'overfitting') to match BTC — quants flatly say it 'can't predict' BTC

No anchor for the elasticity going forward: there's no theory pinning beta at 2.65 vs 1.5 vs 1.0, so the CMA's central number is a judgment call dressed as an estimate; the model also says nothing about volatility or correlations directly

Source quality is mixed and tilts promotional: the strongest numeric claims come from a non-peer-reviewed preprint and from sell-side/asset-manager research (Grayscale, CF Benchmarks) with a long book, not from replicated academic work

approaches.name: Quantity Theory of Money / Velocity Equation of Exchange (MV=PT)
approaches.description: Treats Bitcoin as a medium of exchange and values it by inverting the equation of exchange, MV=PT: the aggregate dollar value of the Bitcoin float equals the annual real transaction volume it intermediates (T) divided by its velocity (V), so price per coin = T/(V·M) with M = circulating supply. The applied strand (Burniske, Bank of England's John Lewis) plugs in a target transaction-volume scenario (illicit flows, Visa-scale retail, all electronic payments, or world-GDP) and a velocity assumption to get a "current utility value," then discounts a future utility value back at a high (30-50%) rate to a present price. A 10-15yr CMA falls out as the expected appreciation toward that discounted future-utility value as the probability of the larger transaction-share scenario rises. The academic GE strand (Schilling & Uhlig 2018/2019, JME) instead derives a fundamental pricing equation implying the BTC/USD price is a MARTINGALE once it is an established currency: expected risk-adjusted real return equals the dollar's, i.e. roughly zero real drift, with all the volatility coming from shifting beliefs about future adoption. So under this family a mature-BTC CMA converges to near-fiat real return, and any positive expected appreciation is a one-time, decaying re-rating as adoption probability climbs toward a ceiling, not a perpetual growth rate.
key_drivers: Annual real transaction volume Bitcoin captures (T) — the addressable payments/remittance/illicit-flow base it actually settles, NOT speculative exchange churn (30%+ of on-chain volume is exchange shuttling, not GDP)
Velocity (V) — turnover of the monetary base; assumption is the single most sensitive input. Ranges cited 1 (held as broad money/SoV) to 6.5-14 (Bitcoin means-of-exchange) to 24 (payment-card-like)
Money supply (M) — fixed/known issuance schedule capped at 21M; the only clean, exogenous variable in the identity

Probability-weighted adoption scenario — which transaction-share state the market believes Bitcoin will occupy (illicit-only, Visa-scale, all-electronic, world-currency); price re-rates as this belief shifts
Discount rate (Burniske 30-50%, 3-5x equity) applied to a future utility value to get present rational price
Hodling / dormant-coin fraction — coins held off-market lower effective M and effective V, raising implied price (the SoV-vs-MoE tension inside the same identity)
In the GE model: dollar inflation target / monetary policy and agents' relative impatience, which pin down the martingale and rule out speculative drift
pros: Grounded in a genuine, century-old macro identity (Fisher MV=PT) rather than a fitted curve — it is an accounting identity, so it cannot be 'spuriously cointegrated' the way S2F/Metcalfe are; the critique is about input choice, not the equation

Forces an explicit, falsifiable use-case: you must name the transaction volume and velocity, which exposes that current on-chain economic volume is far too small to justify price — a useful reality check against hype
Velocity is uniquely MEASURABLE on a public blockchain (every transfer is recorded), unlike in fiat economies where V is a residual — lets the model be empirically disciplined rather than assumed

The Schilling-Uhlig martingale result is a rigorous, peer-reviewed (Journal of Monetary Economics) general-equilibrium foundation that correctly predicts LOW long-run real drift and high belief-driven volatility — a sober antidote to perpetual-exponential models
Naturally generates a wide scenario fan (Lewis: ~$19k illicit-only to >$5M world-currency), making the binary, fat-tailed payoff structure explicit rather than hiding it in a point estimate
Internally consistent with a 10-15yr CMA framing: appreciation is a probability-weighted re-rating that must decay as adoption saturates, matching BTC's observed return decay
cons: Velocity is the dominant input and is both unstable and poorly defined — on-chain measures (coin-days-destroyed, NVT) disagree wildly and are contaminated by exchange transfers, mixers, and change outputs; Pernice et al. show common velocity proxies are inferior and not robust. Garbage V → garbage valuation

The identity values Bitcoin ONLY as a medium of exchange and is blind to a pure store-of-value / monetary-premium demand — yet that is empirically the dominant driver of price; coins are increasingly hodled (V collapsing), which the MoE framing reads as bullish but the GE framing reads as Bitcoin failing as money. The model can't cleanly hold both

Adoption as a payment rail has FLATLINED since the late 2010s (Lewis): Lightning never scaled, and stablecoins/instant-payment rails dominate the medium-of-exchange niche without the volatility — so the transaction-volume input is arguably shrinking, not growing

Self-referential / circular: to use Bitcoin for payments you must hold it, but its value comes from transaction demand — high volatility deters payment use, suppressing the very T the valuation needs (the 'endogenous velocity constraint', Soleimani 2025: network architecture structurally caps V)

The discount-back-to-present step (Burniske) smuggles in an arbitrary 30-50% rate and a future-utility scenario that does all the work — the output is whatever T, V, and the scenario probability you assume; even Burniske refuses to use it as a price target

Schilling-Uhlig's martingale conclusion implies ~0% expected REAL appreciation for a mature currency-Bitcoin — directly contradicting the digital-gold appreciation thesis; the family's honest read is that long-run expected real return is near fiat, not exponential

Says almost nothing usable about correlations or volatility magnitude — the GE model gives qualitative 'high belief-driven vol,' the applied model gives a scenario fan, but neither produces a calibrated covariance with equities, gold, or rates

approaches.name: On-Chain Cost-Basis Valuation (Realized Cap / MVRV / SOPR / Thermocap / HODL Waves)
approaches.description: This family values Bitcoin off its aggregate on-chain cost basis rather than any cashflow or supply-scarcity narrative. Realized Cap "pricestamps" every UTXO at the price it last moved and sums them, producing the network's invested-capital base; Realized Price is that per-coin. Market value is then read RELATIVE to this cost basis: MVRV (= MarketCap/RealizedCap) and SOPR measure aggregate unrealized/realized profit, Thermocap measures cumulative miner security spend, and Realized-Cap HODL Waves decompose the cost basis by coin age. Critically, none of these are absolute valuation models — they are mean-reversion OSCILLATORS calibrated to historical cycle extremes (MVRV ~0.8 at bottoms, >3.2 at tops). A 10-15yr CMA does not fall out cleanly: the only structural forward signal is that Realized Cap acts as a slowly-rising floor (it draws down only -14% to -23% when spot falls -75% to -92%), so a CMA must be built by projecting the growth rate of invested capital (net capital inflow) and assuming MVRV mean-reverts toward ~1.5-2x over a full cycle rather than by reading any point figure off the chart.
key_drivers: Realized Cap = cumulative realized profit minus realized loss = net USD capital ever locked into the network (the invested-capital base / on-chain cost basis)
Realized Price = Realized Cap / circulating supply (aggregate holder cost basis per coin); functions as a soft floor
MVRV ratio = Market Cap / Realized Cap = aggregate unrealized-profit multiple; mean-reverting oscillator (bottoms ~0.8, tops ~3.2-3.7)
MVRV Z-Score = (MarketCap - RealizedCap)/stdev(MarketCap); normalizes extremes for cross-cycle comparison
SOPR (Spent Output Profit Ratio) = realized price of spent coins / price paid; >1 = supply in profit being sold, <1 = capitulation
Thermocap = cumulative USD value of all block rewards + fees ever paid to miners (aggregate security spend); Market-Cap/Thermocap is an on-chain 'P/E'-style ratio
Realized-Cap HODL Waves = age-banded decomposition of Realized Cap (who holds cost basis, long-term vs short-term holders)
Net capital inflow / 'realized cap growth rate' — the only variable that drives a long-horizon trajectory rather than a cyclical signal
pros: Grounded in observable on-chain ledger data (UTXO move-prices), not a narrative or fitted regression — Realized Cap is an accounting identity, not a model assumption

Realized Cap / Realized Price empirically behaves as a rising floor: it has fallen only ~-14% to -23% in bear markets vs spot's -75% to -92%, giving a genuine downside-anchor concept useful for tail/loss-given-bear estimation

MVRV/SOPR oscillators have real ex-post discriminating power at extremes — readings have repeatedly bracketed cycle tops and bottoms (MVRV<1 ≈ ~15% of days marked capitulation, MVRV>3.2 ≈ cycle peaks)
Cost-basis framing maps cleanly to investor behavior (mean reversion toward what holders paid), so it is a behaviorally-honest middleware even if not a CMA
Thermocap ties valuation to a real economic floor (energy/security spend), giving an independent cross-check on the cost-basis story
Unlike Stock-to-Flow and Metcalfe, this family does NOT publish a single point-forecast, so it is harder to weaponize into a spurious 10yr target — its honesty is a feature
cons: Fundamentally an OSCILLATOR, not a valuation model: it tells you where price sits relative to cost basis, never where cost basis (or price) should be in 10-15 years. There is no native long-horizon expected-return output — any CMA is grafted on by the analyst.

Reflexive/circular: Realized Cap is a transformation of past PRICE (each coin stamped at its move-time price). High prices raise realized cap which raises the 'floor' — so the floor is endogenous to the bubble, not an independent fundamental. A permanent 70% drawdown would drag realized price down with it over time.

Thresholds are data-mined on a tiny sample (2-3 full cycles): MVRV>3.7 'overvalued', Z>6.5 'top', M/T~0.000004 'top' are curve-fits with severe lookahead bias and small-n overfitting. Each cycle has hit LOWER MVRV peaks (2013 ~5.7 → later cycles <3) — the calibration visibly decays, mirroring the S2F/Metcalfe post-2021 break critique. Naive use is unsafe.

Predictive performance degrades post-2017/post-futures as markets became more efficient (academic backtests of cost-basis oscillators show Sharpe collapse after 2017); ETF/institutional custody also breaks the on-chain signal because coins move off-chain into wrappers and stop pricestamping.
Supply-side metric noise: lost coins, exchange/wrapper consolidation, and ETF custody distort UTXO age and cost-basis attribution, biasing realized cap and HODL waves.

No correlation, volatility, or cross-asset structure is produced at all — the framework is silent on every CMA covariance input. It cannot, by itself, populate a correlation matrix vs equities/gold/TIPS.

approaches.name: Cross-Sectional Factor & Macro-Liquidity Regression
approaches.description: This family treats BTC as a risk asset whose returns are decomposed by regression onto priced factors rather than valued from cashflows or scarcity. Two strands: (1) the cross-sectional/asset-pricing strand (Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu) builds crypto-native factors — a crypto market factor (CMKT), size (CSIZE) and momentum (CMOM), plus network-adoption and investor-attention proxies — and shows a 3-factor model spans the cross-section of coin returns; (2) the macro-liquidity strand (Onramp, post-ETF studies) regresses BTC on global M2, the dollar (DXY) and real rates. A 10-15yr CMA does NOT fall out of these models directly: they are descriptive/explanatory (what moves BTC, and how much variance loads on each factor) rather than predictive of a long-run level. To get a CMA you must feed the regression long-run factor-premium and factor-path assumptions (an equity-risk-premium-style estimate for the crypto market factor, plus a view on the secular liquidity/adoption path) and let the betas translate them — which is why the expected-return output is inherited from the analyst's factor views, not produced by the model.
key_drivers: Crypto market factor (CMKT) — the dominant systematic driver; coin betas to the aggregate crypto market explain most cross-sectional variation
Size factor (CSIZE) — small-cap coins earn a premium; BTC as the largest coin loads negatively, implying lower expected excess return than the alt-coin universe
Momentum factor (CMOM) — strong time-series and cross-sectional momentum; 1-4 week momentum predicts returns (a behavioral/attention driver, not a fundamental one)
Investor-attention / sentiment proxies (Google/social search, flows) — Liu-Tsyvinski find attention strongly forecasts short-horizon returns
Network-adoption factors (active addresses, users) — priced; production-cost factors (hashrate/mining) are NOT priced
Macro-liquidity trio: global M2 (liquidity impulse), USD/DXY, and real yields (discount rate) — weak monthly link, materially stronger at 6-24m horizons
Post-ETF institutionalization — rising loading on the equity/growth (Nasdaq) factor as ETF/corporate flows tie BTC to quarterly equity rebalancing
pros: Empirically grounded and falsifiable — uses standard asset-pricing machinery (Fama-MacBeth, GRS tests, rolling betas) rather than curve-fitting a price level
Correctly characterizes BTC's risk profile: high idiosyncratic/crypto-specific variance, low historical loading on traditional macro factors — directly informative for the correlation cells of a CMA
Captures regime change: the macro-liquidity and post-ETF strands document BTC's rising equity beta and near-zero gold correlation, which a static historical correlation would miss
Honest about predictability: the academic strand attributes short-horizon predictability to attention/momentum (behavioral), not to a fundamental anchor — avoids over-claiming
Separates systematic from idiosyncratic — useful for portfolio construction (how much BTC risk is diversifiable vs priced)
cons: Does NOT produce a long-run expected return on its own — it is descriptive; the CMA appreciation number is smuggled in via an assumed crypto-market-factor premium, so the model launders the analyst's prior rather than generating a forecast

Short, regime-shifting sample: factor premia (esp. CMKT and CMOM) are estimated on ~2014-2022 data dominated by a secular bull market; out-of-sample momentum/size premia in equities have decayed, and there is no reason crypto premia are stable over 10-15yr
Betas are unstable: the very post-ETF literature it relies on shows BTC's equity beta jumping from ~0 to 0.5-0.9, so any CMA built on a point-estimate beta is fragile
The macro-liquidity link is weak month-to-month and the firm-published (Onramp) version is marketing-adjacent — it reports regime medians, not betas, and avoids point forecasts

Naive scarcity/network cousins (Stock-to-Flow, naive Metcalfe) are statistically REJECTED — S2F is spurious regression on two non-stationary, non-cointegrated series with autocorrelated residuals; Metcalfe transaction-count effects are insignificant/negative once autocorrelation and endogeneity are corrected, and both break post-2021. A factor-regression CMA must not borrow their implied appreciation paths
High multicollinearity / small-N: with only BTC (not a panel) the macro regressions have few independent observations at the 6-24m horizons where the signal allegedly lives, inviting overfitting

approaches.name: Options-Implied Risk-Neutral Forward & Vol Surface (Deribit DVOL / RND)
approaches.description: This approach extracts what the listed BTC options market prices: a risk-neutral (Q-measure) forward and a full implied-volatility surface (Deribit DVOL is the VIX-style 30-day variance-swap distillation of that surface). From the cross-section of strikes one recovers a risk-neutral density (RND) of the terminal price; from the term structure one reads the market's annualized vol expectation by tenor. Crucially, the risk-neutral forward equals spot times cost-of-carry (futures basis / funding) — under Q the drift is the financing rate, NOT a real-world expected return — so the options surface delivers volatility and a no-arbitrage forward but says nothing directly about 10-15yr appreciation. A CMA only "falls out" if you (a) extrapolate the (downward-sloping, short-dated) vol term structure to a 10-15yr horizon, and (b) graft on a real-world risk premium from a separate P-density estimate (e.g. Martin/Chabi-Yo lower bounds), since the options alone are silent on drift.
key_drivers: Implied volatility surface (level, skew, term structure) across Deribit/CME strikes and expiries
Risk-neutral forward = spot x cost-of-carry (futures basis / perpetual funding rate); the Q-drift is the risk-free/financing rate, not expected return
Risk-neutral density (RND) shape from the second derivative of call prices vs strike (Breeden-Litzenberger) — fat right tail, lognormal-plus-jump
Variance risk premium: gap between implied (Q) and realized (P) variance, the wedge that must be modeled to get from price to physical return
Pricing kernel / risk-aversion needed to convert Q-density to P-density and thus recover an expected return (Almeida-Grith-Miftachov; Martin lower bound)
Option liquidity and longest-available tenor — caps the horizon at which the surface is observable (months, not years)
pros: Purely market-implied and forward-looking: aggregates the positioning of sophisticated option traders in real time, no backward-looking sample dependence
Best-in-class for the VOLATILITY input of a CMA — DVOL and the term structure give a clean, daily, tradeable estimate of expected vol, far better grounded than a historical stdev
No-arbitrage discipline: the forward and RND are internally consistent and replicable, immune to the spurious-regression problems that plague S2F/Metcalfe
Captures the full distribution (skew, kurtosis, crash risk), not just a point — useful for tail-aware / left-tail CMA scenario work

The RND-vs-realized comparison yields a defensible variance risk premium and, with a pricing-kernel assumption, an option-implied expected-return lower bound (Almeida et al. ~66%/yr at 1mo; Martin bound 65.6%) — a genuinely market-anchored premium number
Galaxy and desks use it precisely as a 'maturing into a macro asset' read: the surface's flattening/declining vol IS the decay signal a forward CMA needs
cons: Fundamentally cannot produce an expected appreciation. The risk-neutral forward drifts at the risk-free/funding rate by construction; equating that to a CMA return implies ~0% real appreciation, which is economically wrong for the asset. Any appreciation figure must be imported from a separate model — the options surface is silent on drift. This is the central, disqualifying limitation for a return CMA.

Horizon mismatch is severe: liquid BTC options extend ~6 months (Deribit) to ~12-13 months (CME, through next December); there is NO 10-15yr option. Extrapolating a 30-day DVOL or a 6-month surface to a 10-15yr CMA is a heroic, unvalidated stretch — the term structure is estimated, not observed, at the relevant horizon.

The P-density / pricing-kernel step that rescues an expected return is fragile: estimates swing from ~44% to ~102%/yr across vol regimes (Almeida-Grith-Miftachov), are only 27-day horizon, and assume the short-dated risk premium persists — exactly the assumption a maturing-asset CMA should reject.
Variance risk premium is large and time-varying (1mo VRP collapsed from ~15% to ~2.5% around the 2024 halving), so even the vol read is regime-dependent and can overstate forward vol.

Risk-neutral != physical: short-dated RNDs are dominated by hedging/skew demand and crash insurance, not long-run fundamentals — using them as a 10yr distribution conflates options demand with macro expectation.
Liquidity/venue concentration (Deribit dominant, now Coinbase-owned) and thin deep-OTM long-dated strikes make the long end of any extrapolated surface noisy and manipulable.

Marketing risk: 'options imply $250k' headlines (Galaxy 2026) are wide risk-neutral ranges, NOT directional forecasts; the same surface assigns near-equal odds to $50k and $250k by end-2026. Treating the high tail as an expected value launders a vol read into a return claim.

approaches.name: Equilibrium / Game-Theoretic Security-Utility Pricing
approaches.description: This family treats Bitcoin not as a cash-flow asset but as a token whose fundamental value is the present value of a stream of net transactional benefits (Biais et al., JoF 2023) and/or the equilibrium price that simultaneously clears asset demand and induces enough mining hashrate to keep the chain secure against attack (Chen 2024 security-utility Nash equilibrium; Houy 2014; Alden's fee-based security model). Value is endogenous: today's price depends on expected future prices (because transactional usefulness and security both scale with price), which yields a self-referential fixed point. A 10-15yr CMA does NOT fall out cleanly — these models are explicitly positive (explaining price formation and volatility) rather than normative forecasts. The one robust quantitative takeaway is decompositional: in calibration, only a minority of Bitcoin return variance maps to changes in net transactional benefits; the majority is "extrinsic" / sunspot volatility, so any point forecast inherits enormous uncertainty and the models predict perpetual high vol and multiple equilibria rather than a single expected return.
key_drivers: Net transactional benefits: the flow utility of holding/using BTC for transactions and store-of-value, indexed empirically (Biais et al.)
Self-referential fixed point: fundamental value depends on future prices, generating multiple equilibria and sunspot (extrinsic) volatility even with constant fundamentals
Security budget = block subsidy + transaction fees; must remain large enough that cost-to-attack > attack payoff (Chen, Houy, Alden)
Endogenous hashrate via free-entry zero-profit miner condition: F^-1(H) = P*(B+Phi)/H
Halving dynamics: as block subsidy B -> 0, security must be carried by fees Phi; viability of the fee market is the central open question
Attack-cost / security-utility coupling: higher price -> larger security budget -> more attack resistance -> supports demand (reflexive loop)
Fixed supply Q clears against speculative + transactional demand D(P, security)
pros: Genuinely peer-reviewed (Journal of Finance) and microfounded; derives value from first principles rather than curve-fitting, unlike S2F/Metcalfe
Honestly explains why BTC is so volatile: multiple equilibria + sunspots are a feature of the model, not noise to be assumed away
Provides a falsifiable lower-bound discipline — the chain is only worth holding if the fee-funded security budget can deter attack as subsidy decays, tying long-run value to real adoption/fee demand
Avoids the 'no cashflow so unvaluable' dead-end by identifying transactional-benefit and security streams as the economic substitute for cashflow
Comparative statics (halving lowers P and H together; fee market must develop) give a coherent narrative for the appreciation-decay path
cons: Produces essentially NO usable point CMA: no closed-form steady-state price, no expected-return number, no volatility forecast, no correlation outputs — the papers explicitly decline to forecast
Multiple-equilibria / sunspot result means the model is consistent with almost any price path, which is intellectually honest but useless for a single 10-15yr expected return

The fee-based-security terminal state is unsolved: Chen, Houy and Alden all flag 'whether fee demand can fund security' as an OPEN question — the long-run equilibrium may not exist or may be fragile (tragedy-of-the-commons free-riding on security)
Net-transactional-benefit indices are noisy proxies; calibration shows fundamentals explain only a minority of return variance, so the 'fundamental' anchor is weak
Reflexivity (price -> security -> value) makes the model prone to self-fulfilling collapse as well as boom; it does not pin down which equilibrium prevails

These academic models are frequently conflated in marketing with S2F/Metcalfe, which the literature largely REJECTS as spurious: S2F is a regression of two non-stationary series (spurious cointegration, serially correlated residuals) that broke decisively post-2021 (predicted ~$100k+ in 2022, BTC crashed); naive Metcalfe network-value fits are likewise overfit and non-robust. Do not let the rigorous equilibrium work launder the discredited scarcity/network curves.

approaches.name: Discounted-Utility / Monetary-Premium DCF (Moneyness Analogue)
approaches.description: This family forces Bitcoin into a DCF-style frame even though it has no cashflow, by treating its "moneyness" — the utility flow from serving store-of-value / medium-of-exchange / unit-of-account functions — as an implicit dividend, then discounting a terminal monetary-premium value. Two academic sub-strands exist. (1) A market-to-fundamental ratio strand (Liu & Zhang's Price-to-Utility / PU ratio) proxies the store-of-value "utility" via on-chain UTXO staking ratios and asks whether price is rich or cheap to that utility, predicting LONG-horizon (not short) returns via mean-reversion of the ratio. (2) A unified-discounting strand (Papadogiannis; "Valuing Scarcity") models scarcity as a latent state variable whose "monetization function" maps into pseudo-cashflows or a terminal resale value, discounted at an effective rate c_eff = f(benchmark cost of capital c, belief-distortion ratio K). A 10–15yr CMA does not fall out cleanly: the model yields a fair-value LEVEL (or a rich/cheap signal), and an expected return only emerges by assuming the price-to-utility ratio mean-reverts AND the underlying utility/TAM grows along an adoption S-curve — i.e., the CMA is really a TAM-penetration forecast wearing DCF clothing.
key_drivers: Utility/moneyness proxy growth — on-chain activity, active addresses, transaction value, and UTXO staking ratio (Liu-Zhang use staking ratio as the store-of-value proxy)
Total addressable market (TAM) of the monetary functions BTC competes for — gold, offshore/store-of-value wealth, FX/settlement, central-bank reserves — and BTC's penetration share of each
Effective discount rate c_eff = benchmark opportunity cost c times belief-distortion ratio K (Papadogiannis); a very high required return reflecting adoption/survival risk
Probability of monetary adoption / survival — implicit Pr(BTC becomes a durable global store of value) that scales the terminal value
Mean-reversion speed of the market-to-fundamental (PU) ratio — converts a level signal into an expected return
Terminal resale / monetary-premium value at horizon end (no perpetuity of cashflows; value is entirely the terminal moneyness stock)
Macro/liquidity regime — real rates and money-supply growth shift the convenience yield on a non-yielding monetary asset
pros: Honest about the absence of cashflow — instead of faking a dividend it explicitly models a utility/monetary-premium flow or a terminal scarcity value, which is the economically correct object for a non-productive asset

Provides a falsifiable rich/cheap signal: the PU ratio is empirically shown to predict LONG-horizon BTC returns out-of-sample and to beat buy-and-hold and naive market-timing in backtests (Liu & Zhang)
Grounds the proxy in classic monetary theory (medium-of-exchange / store-of-value / unit-of-account) and unique blockchain accounting (UTXO), rather than ad hoc curve-fitting

The unified-discounting variant (Papadogiannis) restores algebraic comparability with equities/gold under one DCF identity, which is exactly what a CMA committee needs to slot BTC next to other building blocks

Naturally accommodates appreciation DECAY: as the TAM penetration S-curve flattens and the PU ratio normalizes, implied forward returns fall toward a gold-like drift — the right shape for a 10–15yr CMA
cons: Garbage-in: the 'utility' proxy is a choice, not a fact. UTXO staking ratios, active addresses, and on-chain volume are gameable, regime-dependent, and only loosely tied to monetary value; the PU ratio's predictive edge is in-sample/backtest and over a short, bull-dominated history (2011–2020).

It is TAM-penetration forecasting in DCF costume. The number that drives everything — Pr(adoption) and terminal share of gold/FX/reserves — is an unfalsifiable prior. Marketing 'academic' DCFs (ARK $1.2–2.4M by 2030; VanEck $2.9M by 2050 ~15% CAGR) are sensitive almost entirely to the penetration assumption, not the discounting math.

Sibling naive models are REJECTED by the peer-reviewed econometrics. Stock-to-Flow regressions are spurious: S2F and price are both non-stationary (I(1)/trending), Engle–Granger cointegration fails its own preconditions, residuals are serially correlated, and the model broke post-2021 (predicted ~$100k in 2022; BTC crashed). Metcalfe/PM ratios likewise have little short-run predictive power and treat all users identically. The PU-ratio paper itself concedes traditional fundamental-to-market ratios fail short-term.

The effective discount rate c_eff and belief-distortion K (Papadogiannis) are not independently observable — they are calibrated to fit observed price, so the framework can rationalize almost any valuation ex post (low falsifiability).

No native volatility or correlation output. The family produces a fair-value level / expected return; vol and the correlation vector must be imported from realized data or asserted — so it contributes nothing to the risk side of a CMA on its own.

Survivorship and reflexivity: 'utility' rises with price (more holders/activity when number-go-up), so utility-as-fundamental and price are mutually endogenous — undercutting the claim that one anchors the other.

cited_outputs.appreciation_nominal: n/a (academic PU/scarcity papers publish fair-value/relative-value signals, not a 10-15yr annualized CMA). Marketing cousins in the same family that DO publish a number: VanEck ~15%/yr nominal to 2050 (base $2.9M); ARK ~53%/yr base / 32% bear / 72% bull CAGR to 2030.

The model treats gold as the primary TAM BTC penetrates, so by construction it needs BTC and gold to share a debasement/real-rate factor — yet realized co-movement is only intermittently and mildly positive, averaging ~0. This is the load-bearing contradiction: you cannot value BTC off gold's TAM (which assumes substitution / co-movement) while observing near-zero realized gold correlation. I keep it at the bottom of the 0.0-0.15 band, not the high correlation the moneyness narrative implies.

approaches.name: Adoption S-Curve / Logistic Demand Growth
approaches.description: This approach models Bitcoin not as a discounted-cashflow asset (it has none) but as a network good whose value is a function of adoption. Demand is assumed to diffuse along a logistic S-curve borrowed from prior technology-diffusion analogs (internet, mobile phones, automobiles, social media), and network size is mapped to value via a Metcalfe-type link (value scales roughly with users^~1.5-2) and/or a fixed total-addressable-market the asset is converging on (a share of monetary gold's ~$15-22T cap, or a fraction of global savings/M2). A 10-15yr CMA falls out mechanically: you posit a terminal adoption level and date (e.g. Blockware's 10% of population by 2030 off a 60% net-entity CAGR; Timmer's ~25% of monetary gold), draw the logistic path to it, convert end-state network size or TAM share into a terminal price, and annualize from spot. Crucially the same logic that produces large near-term multiples also forces appreciation to DECELERATE as you climb the curve toward the inflection and saturation, so the forward 10-15yr CAGR is far below realized history.
key_drivers: Terminal addressable market (TAM): share of monetary gold (~$6T at 25% per Timmer), or share of global M2 / savings / sovereign reserves
Adoption ceiling and timing: terminal user/entity penetration (e.g. 10% of population by 2030) and the date of the logistic inflection point
Net-entity / user growth rate (Blockware: ~60% trailing-10yr CAGR of cumulative net entity growth), which is itself decaying
Metcalfe exponent linking users to value (theoretical 2; empirically estimated ~1.5-1.69, and contested)
Diffusion analog chosen (internet/mobile = gentler slope; social media/smartphones = steeper) — the analog choice dominates the answer
Real interest rates and monetary inflation as a demand multiplier on the adoption curve (Timmer overlays -2% to +2.5% real-rate regimes)
Supply scarcity / issuance decay (halvings) and ETF-driven float reduction as a demand-side amplifier (Standard Chartered, Grayscale)
Per-coin price derived from terminal market cap / circulating (effectively fixed ~21M) supply
pros: Honest about the asset's nature: it values a no-cashflow network on adoption + monetary demand rather than forcing a DCF that cannot exist
Mechanically transparent and decomposable — terminal TAM, adoption ceiling, timing, and Metcalfe exponent are each separately debatable and stress-testable

Naturally produces appreciation DECAY: as penetration rises toward the inflection/saturation, marginal new adoption falls and CAGR compresses, which matches realized history (142%->65%->17%) and is the correct shape for a 10-15yr forward CMA
TAM-share framing (e.g. fraction of monetary gold or global savings) gives a defensible, bounded ceiling rather than open-ended extrapolation
Used by serious institutions (Fidelity/Timmer, Grayscale, Standard Chartered) with explicit macro overlays (real rates, money supply), not just price extrapolation
Internally consistent with a 'digital gold' thesis: ties terminal value to a recognizable store-of-value benchmark
cons: The Metcalfe link to value is largely REJECTED by peer-reviewed work: regressions of price on users are spurious (both series non-stationary/trending; significance vanishes under time fixed-effects; IV studies find the transaction-count effect insignificant or negative across PoW coins) — naive Metcalfe valuation launders autocorrelation as causation

The companion S2F supply model is similarly discredited: halvings act as structural breaks, the fit collapses out-of-sample (Plan-B paths missed badly post-2021), and the apparent fit largely reflects correlation with log-time-since-genesis (~80% Pearson)

Answer is dominated by unfalsifiable analog choice and terminal-date assumptions — choosing 'social media' vs 'landline' adoption slopes swings the price target by an order of magnitude with no objective tie-breaker
Survivorship/selection bias in analogs: only technologies that DID saturate are used; the curve assumes success rather than testing it
No native volatility or correlation output — the framework is a point/path price target, so vol and all cross-asset correlations must be imported from realized data or judgment
Practitioner targets are promotional and serially revised (Standard Chartered cut 2026 target $300K->$150K->$100K within months), so 'cited' numbers are unstable and not CMA-grade

Confuses a long-run equilibrium ceiling with a forward expected return: even if the $1M+ TAM is right, the probability-weighted and time-discounted CMA is much lower, and the models rarely present a true expectation (Timmer himself calls them 'not predictions')
Adoption can stall or reverse (regulation, a superior protocol, loss of the store-of-value narrative); logistic curves have no mechanism for de-adoption
